aggressive_definition: High-grade prostate cancer; the abstract does not report the grade threshold used.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: When stratified by disease severity, dietary folate and folate from natural sources were associated with reduced risk of high-grade cancer as compared to both clinic controls (P for a linear trend = 0.0009 and 0.02, respectively) and biopsy negative controls (P for a linear trend = 0.03 and 0.05, respectively).
study_design: Case-control study with biopsy-confirmed prostate cancer cases, age-matched clinic controls, and negative prostate biopsy controls
cohort_total_n_excerpt: We investigated folate as a risk factor for prostate cancer among 140 biopsy-confirmed prostate cancer patients, 230 age-matched clinic controls, and 250 negative prostate biopsy controls.
reason: The case-control study analyzed overall prostate cancer risk and separately analyzed high-grade prostate cancer risk. The number of high-grade cases and effect estimates with confidence intervals are not reported in the abstract.
